🚨⚽ US BANS AFRICA'S BEST REFEREE FROM THE WORLD CUP IT'S HOSTING

Omar Abdulkadir Artan — CAF's 2025 Referee of the Year, the first Somali official ever selected for a World Cup — denied entry to the United States. He had a valid visa. Somalia is on Trump's expanded travel ban list.

FIFA confirmed he "will not be able to train or officiate at the 2026 World Cup" and added: "FIFA does not intervene in the immigration processes of the host country, including the granting of visas."

A country hosting the world's tournament while banning officials from the world.

🚨🇺🇸 TRUMP BOOED THUNDEROUSLY AT NBA FINALS — CLAIMS IT WAS "MOSTLY CHEERS"

First sitting US president to attend an NBA Finals game. Madison Square Garden. National anthem. Camera pans to Trump saluting — and 20,000 New Yorkers erupt into boos so loud the White House pool report called them "loud and long."

The booing only stopped when the camera cut to Jalen Brunson on the court. That got cheers.

Trump afterward: "It was, I think, mostly cheers."

It was not mostly cheers.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO AUTO PRODUCTION CAUGHT BY TRUMP TARIFFS — BUT EXPORTS AND DOMESTIC SALES STILL GREW</u>

INEGI's May numbers landed: Mexico produced 342,926 light vehicles, down 3.70% year-over-year — Trump tariff drag is real. But the part the gringo press won't lead with: exports STILL grew 4.95% to 127,107 units, and domestic sales also climbed 4.95% versus May 2025.

Year-to-date exports hit 1,388,236 units, up 4.01% on last year — 53,569 MORE Mexican-made vehicles shipped abroad through May. The US still absorbed 75.4% of them.

Translation: Trump can slap tariffs all he wants, the global market still buys what Mexico builds. The neoliberals spent 30 years calling Mexican industry incompetent; turns out it's the only thing standing between the US consumer and a 20% price hike on every vehicle on the lot.

Source: El Financiero / Infobae

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>SHEINBAUM ANNOUNCES 93-BILLION-PESO PETROCHEMICAL REVIVAL IN VERACRUZ — REVERSING 30 YEARS OF NEOLIBERAL DISMANTLING</u>

President Sheinbaum unveiled a 93-billion-peso plan (2025-2030) to reactivate Mexico's petrochemical industry across six Pemex complexes in Veracruz — the heart of the sector neoliberalism left rotting since the 90s. Target: 849,000 metric tons of petrochemicals and 4 million metric tons of fertilizers per year, all produced at home instead of imported.

The breakdown — 30B pesos for ethane-ethylene rehab, 13B for ammonia, 13.7B for Fertinal-ProAgro, 11B for aromatics, plus a brand-new urea granule plant (Escolín Project).

Energy Secretary Luz Elena González put the point bluntly: the plan focuses on "domestically-produced chemical inputs currently imported." That's sovereignty as industrial policy — chemicals, fertilizers, food chain — all back in Mexican hands. Governor Rocío Nahle noted Sheinbaum has visited Veracruz 14 times. She's not announcing things. She's rebuilding.

Source: Regeneración

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"QrGATE" — PRI CAUGHT BUYING VOTES IN COAHUILA WITH QR CODES, MORENA DOCUMENTS THE SCHEME</u>

Morena national leader Ariadna Montiel just dropped the receipts on what she's calling "QrGate": a vote-buying operation in Sunday's Coahuila election where the PRI distributed QR codes to voters, who then photographed their marked ballot next to the code so the image could be scanned on a mobile platform — and the payment released.

Montiel says the scheme "could surpass at the state level what we knew in the 2012 election of Peña Nieto" — the Soriana and Monex cards. Complaints are going to the Coahuila Electoral Institute and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

The PRI-led alliance walked off with 16 districts and 684,515 votes (55%). With Alito Moreno at the helm, the same party that institutionalized Monex-Soriana now just industrialized it on a smartphone. Old playbook, new app.

Source: Contralínea

🔥🇲🇽 <u>59 HOMEMADE EXPLOSIVES SEIZED ON BUS HEADED TO CNTE TEACHERS' MARCH</u>

Authorities just intercepted a bus on the Mexico-Cuernavaca highway carrying 59 homemade explosive devices — and the bus was on its way to join today's CNTE teachers' march in CDMX. Inspection happened peacefully with passenger consent after a citizen tip, coordinated with CNDH and the CDMX government.

Arturo Medina, Segob Undersecretary of Human Rights: "Estamos a favor de la manifestación pacífica, pero no se debe poner en riesgo a la población."

Read it slowly: bombs. On a bus. Disguised inside a teachers' protest. Eleven days before Mexico hosts the World Cup. Sheinbaum has been saying for a week the provocation isn't coming from the teachers — it's coming from groups who NEED a repression headline before the international cameras land. There's the smoking gun.

Source: Contralínea

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>UN HUMAN RIGHTS CHIEF DEMANDS US LIFT CUBA SANCTIONS — INFANT MORTALITY HAS DOUBLED</u>

UN High Commissioner Volker Türk publicly broke from Washington today and demanded the US immediately lift the sanctions Trump tightened on Cuba since January 2026, citing collapse of essential services and child deaths.

The numbers Türk put on the record: infant mortality on the island has DOUBLED to 9.9 deaths per 1,000 births. Childhood cancer survival has crashed from 85% to 65%. Blackouts exceed 20 hours a day. Oncology, dialysis, maternal health all gasping.

Türk: "There are children dying because doctors do not have access to essential medical supplies and medicines. This is unacceptable."

Mexico has been the only neighbor on the right side — Sembrando Vida still in Cuba, fuel and humanitarian aid still flowing. The blockade is policy-murder of children. The UN just said it.

Source: La Jornada / Infobae

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DHS BLOWS UP TRUMP-ADMIN NARRATIVE: NO "SPECIAL PERMITS" FOR DURAZO OR VILLARREAL</u>

The US Department of Homeland Security confirmed in writing to La Opinión that Sonora governor Alfonso Durazo and Tamaulipas governor Américo Villarreal have NOT been granted any "parole for significant public benefit" — directly contradicting the LA Times story Trump's circle planted in January claiming both had visas revoked but secret permits to keep flying in.

DHS reply: "Francisco Alfonso Durazo Montaño and Américo Villarreal Anaya have not been [benefited with such permission]."

Sheinbaum nailed it from Palacio Nacional: the leaks are "narratives pushed by sectors seeking to affect the bilateral relationship between Mexico and the United States." Translation: the soft-coup playbook keeps recycling. The paper said it. DHS killed it.

Source: La Jornada
